posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I wonder if next summer I took a hologram and layed it on my untanned stomach and layed out in the sun till I was red, if I would get a hologram? Can the skin/sun have a high enough resolution?

Then how would the fringes shift when I turned from red to bronze?

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: The size of a human cell is about 15um. The grain size in pfg-01 is 40nm, about 400 times smaller. So, to me it seems unlikely.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Yes, this was one of those brain burps that I posted without giving much thought to.

You see, I constantly look for things or materials in the every day world that change color or darken when exposed to light.

posts.author: Vidar
posts.content_md: Even if the skin had enough resolution would not this "setup" require a single wavelength illumination source? Making contact copies still require the use of a laser, right? On the grotesque side, have you ever thought about how you would replay the resulting transmission skinnogram?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Yes, this is and example of the old problem I have been poondering over for years.

It seems you have to have transmission to make/or view a hologram. 

Transmission Hologram: Record - Non Transmission ... Replay Transmission

Reflection Hologram: Record - Tranmission ... Replay Non Transmisson.

Basically, I am not aware of anyway to make and view a hologram on an opaque object.
